items.title: Madras High Court bars Blinkit from using CSK fan Saravanan Hari’s persona without consent
items.summary: The Madras High Court has restrained Blinkit, The Times of India and other unknown defendants from using Chennai Super Kings' fan Saravanan Hari’s persona without his written permission. Justice PB Balaji passed the order granting interim relief in the personality rights suit instituted by Saravanan over the use of a cartoon figure by Blinkit allegedly resembling him. The Court also directed Blink Commerce Private Limited and Bennett, Coleman & Company Limited (Times of India's publisher) to preserve and produce materials relating to the disputed advertisement, including artwork, design records, emails and correspondence with designers or external vendors. Justice PB Balaji Saravanan sought damages of ₹1.1 crore for the alleged unauthorised commercial exploitation of his distinctive appearance. The dispute concerned a full-page Blinkit advertisement published in the Chennai edition of The Sunday Times of India on March 23, 2025.
